formulas.purpose: Cement, sand and aggregate volumes for a wet concrete volume, from the caller's own mix proportions, a dry-volume factor and a waste share.

not_to_be_confused_with.difference: cost_buildup_concrete prices a cubic metre of concrete; concrete_mix_proportions gives material volumes, not money.

formulas.purpose: Selling price per cubic metre of concrete and the value of a given volume, built from material prices and contents, per-m3 plant, labour, erection, power and indirect lines, waste, indirect share and markup.

not_to_be_confused_with.difference: concrete_mix_proportions gives material volumes from mix parts; cost_buildup_concrete gives a price.
concrete_volume measures the cubic metres; cost_buildup_concrete takes them as quantity_m3.

formulas.purpose: Selling price per square metre of formwork and the value of a given area, from shuttering supply, scaffold hire over the cycle, labour hours, crane time, indirect share and markup.

not_to_be_confused_with.difference: cost_buildup_concrete is per cubic metre of concrete; cost_buildup_formwork is per square metre of formed face.

formulas.purpose: Selling price per tonne of reinforcement and the value of a given mass in kg, from material price, waste, labour hours, crane hours, indirect share and markup.

not_to_be_confused_with.difference: rebar_weight gives the mass of bars; cost_buildup_rebar prices a mass already known, taken in kg.

formulas.purpose: Hire cost of a number of cranes over a number of months: dry hire, optional operator and riggers, a remote-area factor, plus mobilisation and demobilisation.

not_to_be_confused_with.difference: mobilization_cost_estimate is site set-up for personnel (offices, camp, transport); crane_cost_estimate is crane hire only.

formulas.purpose: Bank-volume balance of cut against fill (positive is surplus to export, negative is deficit to import) and the loose volume to haul after bulking.

not_to_be_confused_with.difference: excavation_volume measures one dug volume from its dimensions; cut_fill_balance compares two volumes already measured.

formulas.purpose: Floor, ceiling, skirting and wall-finish quantities of a set of rooms from floor area, perimeter, room count and floor-to-ceiling height, less door and window openings.

not_to_be_confused_with.difference: resource_line_cost prices one line's labour, plant and material; interior_finishes_takeoff only measures quantities.

formulas.purpose: Material required for a quantity of work: the quantity divided by the output per unit of material, times an optional waste factor or percentage.

not_to_be_confused_with.difference: resource_line_cost gives cost and crew-days from a daily output; material_consumption gives a material quantity, not money.

formulas.purpose: Site set-up cost from personnel count and months: monthly per-person rates for offices, camp, transport, safety and IT, one-off set-up costs and demobilisation, at the project's rates.

not_to_be_confused_with.difference: crane_cost_estimate is crane hire; mobilization_cost_estimate is people and site facilities.

formulas.purpose: Bar length and mass of reinforcement over a slab or wall area from bar spacing and diameter, one way or both ways.

not_to_be_confused_with.difference: rebar_weight starts from a known bar length or mass; rebar_by_area starts from an area and a spacing.

formulas.purpose: Mass of reinforcing bars of one diameter from their total length (or a count of bars of that length), or the metres run a given mass of that diameter makes.

not_to_be_confused_with.difference: rebar_by_area starts from a slab or wall area and a bar spacing; rebar_weight starts from a known bar length or a known mass.

formulas.purpose: Labour, plant and material split of one estimate line: crew-days from the quantity and the daily output, labour at the day rate, plant as a share of labour, material at a rate per unit.

not_to_be_confused_with.difference: material_consumption gives a material quantity; resource_line_cost gives the line's cost.

knowledge.purpose: The unit each kind of bill item is measured in under the civil and building measurement methods, to read before a quantity is extended against a rate.
How a swelling factor is worked out from Proctor density, compaction and loose density, to read before choosing the bulking of cut to haul.
How interior quantities and their resource costs are derived on this platform, step by step, to read before an interior take-off is priced.

skills.purpose: Review a produced take-off for one trade: revisions first, double counts, missed scope, measurement rules, arithmetic, one evidence field per check; it does not re-measure.
Before a bill or bid is relied on, test the three identities of a priced schedule: quantity times rate equals amount, rows sum to subtotals, subtotals sum to the total; it corrects nothing.

chains.purpose: Price the concrete of a rectangular slab: measure the volume with its waste, then build up the price of that volume.
Price the reinforcement of a slab mesh: bar length over the area from the spacing, the mass of that length, then build up the price of that mass.
